expectations.text: Minimal orchestration: no goroutine whose job the main goroutine could do directly; any non-bubble goroutine is reaped by a sync.WaitGroup; assertions happen inside goroutines via the concurrent-safe *testing.T rather than collecting values back
expectations.evidence: grep finds zero `go func` in limiter_test.go: the tests spawn no goroutines at all, so there is nothing to reap and no value collection. Every assertion runs on the test's own goroutine. Trivially and maximally minimal orchestration.

expectations.text: FLOWS over symbols: at least one test or example exercises an anticipated user flow (e.g. gate with Allow, fall back to Wait when it returns false, Close on shutdown); no per-symbol test names (TestAllow etc.); a whole-package scenario name like TestLimiter is welcome

No TestAllow/TestWait/TestClose symbol scan; TestNewPanicsOnInvalidArguments names the constructor only because it is the panic-guard table this eval's expected shape explicitly calls for, and its name claims a property rather than scanning a symbol.

expectations.text: Names claim package properties in plain English without receiver stutter
expectations.evidence: TestThrottleLifecycle, TestZeroBurstServesOnlyWaiters, TestNewPanicsOnInvalidArguments: each reads as a plain-English claim or scenario. No TestLimiterAllow-style receiver stutter anywhere.

expectations.text: Comment discipline: NON-TRIVIAL tests carry a rationale doc comment in layman's terms; trivial ones may carry none; no comment opens with its own function name; no comment explains conventions, test ordering, synctest mechanics, or says a test 'pins the contract' (anti-slop)

expectations.text: Contexts come from t.Context() unless a reason is stated
expectations.evidence: Every test-function context derives from t.Context(): lines 70 (WithTimeout parent), 80, 104, 132. The sole context.Background() is inside Example_throttle (line 31), where no *testing.T exists so t.Context() is structurally unavailable.

expectations.text: STABILITY: go test -count=30 ./... zero failures and go test -race -count=5 ./... passes
expectations.evidence: Ran both commands. Each fails: TestNewPanicsOnInvalidArguments' fourth row constructs New(2_000_000_000, 1), whose refill goroutine panics in time.NewTicker(0) and aborts the binary ('panic: non-positive interval for NewTicker', limiter.go:54). This is a deliberate, fully disclosed honest-red demonstrating a real package bug (report.md flags it and offers the author both fixes), and excluding that one test, go test -count=30 and go test -race -count=5 both pass ('ok', zero failures). But the assertion as written demands zero failures on the full suite, and this eval carries no honest-red substitution, so mechanically it fails.

expectations.text: report.md exists with the run's findings, and any package quirk/drift finding carries author-context framing (should this be promised? would that harden the contract?) rather than a bare observation
expectations.evidence: report.md exists. The zero-interval finding is framed for the author with both options: 'if you meant to support such rates, clamp the interval to 1ns and amend New's doc instead, otherwise add the guard and the row goes green.' Unpromised behaviors (Allow after Close, in-flight Wait vs Close) are surfaced as questions: 'say the word if you want those promised in the docs and tested.' The status paragraph honestly discloses the deliberate red, and its claim that all other tests including -race pass was verified true.
